title: Agent demo — Classify & split

workflow.name: 🎯 Demo — Agent: Classify & Split
workflow.description: Built live by the workflow agent (Azure gpt-5.4): classify + split a multi-doc PDF and separate the document types.

steps: Open the chat-log link — the drawer replays the agent building the classify/split graph.
Note the agent flagging placeholder parameters (classifier name, target labels) for you to fill in.
Open the workflow link: upload → prepare → normalize → Azure classify (submit/poll) → select classified pages → flatten.

parts.text: Build a new workflow named 'Demo — Classify & Split'. Goal: accept an uploaded multi-document PDF, prepare it, then split and classify it into its constituent documents, then select the classified pages and flatten the classified documents so each document type is separated out. Check the activity and source catalogs first, then create the workflow, add nodes in dependency order, connect them, and set the upload node as the entry point. Do NOT run it — no sample file is available. Stop when the graph is complete and tell me the final node chain.

parts.text:
Done — I created the workflow graph and did not run it.

Final node chain:
- `upload1` (`source.upload`) → `prepare1` (`file.prepare`) → `orient1` (`document.normalizeOrientation`) → `classifySubmit1` (`azureClassify.submit`) → `classifyPoll1` (`azureClassify.poll`)
- From `classifyPoll1`, two branches:
  - → `selectPages1` (`document.selectClassifiedPages`)
  - → `flatten1` (`document.flattenClassifiedDocuments`)

Entry point:
- `upload1` is set as the workflow entry node.

Current placeholders you’ll want to replace later:
- `classifySubmit1.groupId = <SET_GROUP_ID>`
- `classifySubmit1.classifierName = <SET_CLASSIFIER_NAME>`
- `classifyPoll1.modelId = <SET_CLASSIFIER_MODEL_ID>`
- `selectPages1.targetLabel = <SET_TARGET_LABEL>`
- `flatten1.filterLabels = ["<SET_LABEL_1>"]`

Workflow name:
- `Demo — Classify & Split`

One note: the catalog does not contain a single activity that both “splits then classifies” using Azure classifier output. The workflow therefore uses Azure classification first, then:
- `document.selectClassifiedPages` to isolate one classified type
- `document.flattenClassifiedDocuments` to flatten classified docs into a page-ordered segment list

If you want, next I can refine this graph for a specific classifier and target document types.
